About Marquee Sports Network Marquee Sports Network has been the exclusive television home of Chicago Cubs baseball since launching in 2020. The 2026 broadcast team features Jon "Boog" Sciambi on play-by-play — a familiar and beloved voice now entering his sixth season with the network — alongside Jim Deshaies as primary color analyst, a Cubs broadcasting institution who has been calling games on the North Side since 2013. Taylor McGregor and Elise Menaker serve as field reporters, providing in-game sideline coverage and contributing to pregame and postgame programming. Studio coverage is anchored by Cole Wright, a Chicago-area native who hosts Cubs Pregame Live and Cubs Postgame Live alongside a deep bench of former Cubs players and analysts. Marquee airs the vast majority of Chicago's games not claimed by national broadcast windows, making it the centerpiece of any Cubs streaming setup. What About Out-of-Market Cubs Fans? If you live outside the Chicago market and can't access Marquee Sports Network locally, Fubo still has you covered. MLB.TV is available as an add-on through Fubo letting you stream every out-of-market regular season game live and on demand. This is the gold standard for fans following their team from afar, giving you access to all 162 games regardless of where you live. Note that standard MLB.TV blackout restrictions apply: if you're in the Cubs' home market, those games will be blacked out on MLB.TV (which is why Marquee Sports Network via Fubo is the right solution for local fans). The 2026 Cubs: A Team Built to Win The Cubs enter 2026 with genuine championship aspirations after their 92-70 season in 2025 — their best record since 2017 and their first playoff series win since that same year. After defeating the San Diego Padres in the Wild Card Series, the Cubs fell to the Milwaukee Brewers in a hard-fought five-game NLDS. The North Side is hungry for more. The front office responded aggressively. The headline move was the signing of three-time All-Star third baseman Alex Bregman to a 5-year, $175 million deal — the most significant free agent addition Chicago has made in years. A two-time World Series champion and Gold Glove winner, Bregman anchors an already deep infield alongside shortstop Dansby Swanson, second baseman Nico Hoerner, and first baseman Michael Busch — a group that combined for nearly 19 bWAR in 2025 alone. The rotation received a major injection of upside with the trade acquisition of right-hander Edward Cabrera from Miami, who posted career-best numbers in 2025 across ERA, strikeouts, and innings pitched. Cabrera joins re-signed ace Shota Imanaga, the versatile Jameson Taillon, and breakout arm Matthew Boyd — who made the All-Star team in 2025 in his first healthy season in years — to give Craig Counsell one of the deepest starting staffs in the National League. Cade Horton, the 2025 NL Rookie of the Year runner-up, adds even more youth and upside to the mix. Ace Justin Steele is targeting a midseason return from Tommy John surgery, which could supercharge the rotation in the second half. The bullpen was fully rebuilt around veteran free agent additions Phil Maton, Hoby Milner, Jacob Webb, and Hunter Harvey, while closer Daniel Palencia returns to anchor the late innings. In the outfield, Pete Crow-Armstrong — who became the first Cub in history to record 30 home runs, 30 doubles, and 30 stolen bases in a single season last year — is focused on improving his plate discipline alongside veteran left fielder Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki, who drove in 103 runs in 2025. With a loaded rotation, a rebuilt bullpen, and a lineup upgraded by Bregman's championship pedigree, the Cubs are firmly in the conversation for the NL Central crown — making 2026 a season well worth streaming from Opening Day to the final out. 2026 Chicago Cubs Season: Key Dates to Know Spring Training Begins: February 20, 2026 Opening Day: March 26, 2026 (vs. Washington Nationals at Wrigley Field) Jackie Robinson Day: April 15, 2026 All-Star Week: July 11–14, 2026 Home Run Derby: July 13, 2026 Trade Deadline: August 3, 2026 MLB at Field of Dreams: August 13, 2026 Postseason Begins: September 29, 2026 World Series: October 23, 2026 Tips for Streaming the Cubs Like a Pro Start with Fubo as your base — it's one of the only streaming services that carries Marquee Sports Network, making it essential for in-market Cubs fans in the Chicago area. Add MLB.TV as an add-on through Fubo for out-of-market coverage — this gives you every regular season game live and on demand, perfect if you're not in the Chicago market. Add the Sports Plus package for MLB Network — daily baseball programming and select live games make it a worthwhile upgrade for the serious fan. Set up Cloud DVR for doubleheaders and late games — Fubo's Unlimited Cloud DVR lets you record games so you never miss an inning, even on busy nights with overlapping matchups. Check national windows early — the Cubs are regularly featured on FOX Saturday baseball and ESPN weeknight games; these are already included in your Fubo package. Monitor the playoff broadcast schedule in September — postseason rights shift each round, so check which networks have each series and confirm your Fubo plan covers them. How to Stream Every Cubs Game in 2026: The Bottom Line For Cubs fans, the path to streaming every game in 2026 is straightforward: Subscribe to Fubo for Marquee Sports Network (local games), FOX/FS1, ESPN/ESPN2/ABC, and ESPN+ — covering the backbone of the Cubs broadcast schedule. Use Fubo's Unlimited Cloud DVR to record any game you can't watch live.
